spec_items.ref: WN_7 (3no) marked 'AOV' and WL_1 (4no) 'Louvres to smoke shaft' on schedule 52003 - the smoke ventilation function itself
spec_items.treatment: GAP - quoted as ordinary windows, no AOV mechanism priced at all
spec_items.evidence: THE WHOLE OF QT252257 (GBP 7,085.76 cost, GBP 10,055.76 sell) IS THIS PACKAGE, AND NONE OF IT IS PRICED AS SMOKE-CONTROL EQUIPMENT. Schedule 5244-ARK-52003 carries the heading 'AOV SMOKE SHAFT LOUVRE' and the note 'WL_00 Louvres to smoke shaft'. WN_7 x3 sit at Corridor 1-1, 1-2 and 1-3 (levels 1-3), 2100 high x 910 wide, with 'AOV' in the additional-information column. WL_1 x4 sit at levels 0-3, 2100 x 1210. NBS 9001 L20 clause 630 specifies these as COLT PROPRIETARY SMOKE-CONTROL PRODUCTS, every one motorised: 'COLTITE GLAZED LOBBY VENTILATOR (STAIR C) - mounted into prepared openings in the external wall, Type CLT, double glazed with thermally broken glazing and outer frames, nominal size 1000mm wide x 2000mm high or equivalent, DRIVE OPEN/DRIVE CLOSE USING A 24V MOTOR MOUNTED TO THE REAR' (WN_7 at 910 x 2100 is that item's 'or equivalent'); and 'EN SEEFIRE LOUVRED NATURAL VENTILATOR - size to match shaft dimensions, clear opening louvred natural ventilator... DESIGNED AND TESTED TO EN 12101-2... the position of the louvres is controlled by a 24Vdc ELECTRIC ACTUATOR, driven closed by this actuator and opened by a spring'. BSW QUOTED NEITHER. QT252257 quotes 'Qty: 3 Prestige T&T' and 'Qty: 4 Prestige Casement' - ordinary Sheerline windows - and the quote contains ZERO occurrences of AOV, louvre, actuator, chain, stroke, motor, 24V or smoke. WL_1's Glazing line is BLANK and it carries no reinforcing. There is no actuator, no 24V motor, no fire-alarm interface, no control gear and no EN 12101-2 certification anywhere in the price. THE RATES CONFIRM IT: WN_7 is GBP 412.67/m2 over 5.733 m2 and WL_1 is GBP 442.98/m2 over 10.164 m2 - plain-window money. Riverside's only AOV data point (A Plus DualFrame 75Si bottom-hung glazed AOV, 850mm stroke single chain) is GBP 1,401.24/m2 supply, of which the actuator and AOV sash carry roughly GBP 870/m2. On that one point the 3no WN_7 alone are GBP 4,988 to GBP 5,667 of supply cost short. ONE QUOTE, A DIFFERENT SYSTEM, ORDER OF MAGNITUDE ONLY - riverside also confirmed there is no AOV or smoke-vent category anywhere in the rate register, so the 4no louvres cannot be benchmarked at all. Either these 7 units are ours and materially under-priced, or they belong to the smoke-vent specialist and GBP 10,055.76 of sell should come out - our proposal p3 names 'AOV windows, smoke shaft louvres' as part of the tender information and neither prices the function nor excludes it. SIXTH TURN - THE SHAPE OF THIS HAS CHANGED AND THE LOUVRE HALF MAY BE A CREDIT. Fire strategy 5244-ARK-14003 and 14004 rev 02 (09.10.2025) read 'Updated to suit fire officers comments... SMOKE SHAFT OMITTED', and 14005 rev 01 (09.10.2025) reads 'SMOKE SHAFTS OMITTED. MECHANICAL EXTRACT VENT ADDED'. Those sheets were revised three or four more times to rev 04-06 dated 17.02.2026 and the omission was never reversed - the current sheets note a 'Mechanical extract duct through lower ground floor ceiling void' and the only remaining 'Shaft' labels are 1.1-6.2 m2 service and cylinder risers. THE DATES SETTLE IT: window schedules 52001/52002/52003 are dated 08.09.2025 with revision '-' and have NEVER BEEN REVISED; the NBS is 23-08-2025; the shafts went 09.10.2025; the door schedule and fire strategy were updated 17.02.2026. So both documents that put the louvres in our scope predate the omission and neither was updated, while the documents that were updated show the shafts gone. 4no WL_1 at GBP 4,502.40 cost / GBP 6,452.40 sell are scheduled against a shaft deleted five months before the tender was issued - either redundant, or serving the replacement mechanical extract and nobody has said so. AND A SECOND, INDEPENDENT PROBLEM WITH THE 3 AOVs: the current fire strategy legend states the duty as 'AOV. 1.5m2 CLEAR OPENING AREA' (and separately 'SV. NSHEV. 0.4m2 clear opening area minimum'). WN_7 is 910 x 2100 = 1.911 m2 GROSS FRAME, so a 1.5 m2 clear opening would have to be 78.5% of gross - unachievable on the Sheerline 'SP104 70mm Large Outer' T&T that BSW quoted. On the NSHEV reading 0.4 m2 is 20.9% of gross and is fine. Which duty they serve changes the answer and the schedule says 'AOV'. I have NOT computed a clear opening from assumed profile dimensions - BSW must state it. BASIS QUESTION CLOSED: 'clear opening area' is geometric-side language and agrees with the NBS's explicit '1m2 geometric'; 'aerodynamic' appears nowhere in the NBS, mech or electrical specs. SEVENTH TURN CORRECTION: the 78.5%-of-gross figure above overstated the case. riverside established that the APERTURE is the right denominator because the sections eat a fixed share of the gross. From BSW's own stated figures: glass 700 x 1865 = 1.3055 m2 = 87.0% of the 1.5 m2 duty (short 0.1945 m2); frame-internal aperture 770 x 1935 = 1.4900 m2 = 99.3% (short 0.0100 m2, and that takes the 'SP104 70mm Large Outer' section nominally - inferred, not stated). So WN_7 is MARGINAL against 1.5 m2, not clearly incapable. The actuator/motor/fire-alarm-interface absence is unaffected and remains the substantive point; on the NSHEV reading the glass alone is 3.3x the 0.4 m2 duty. My '60% of gross' rule of thumb is WITHDRAWN - it would have condemned a borderline unit.

u_value.required: RESOLVED ON THE TWELFTH TURN. The chain is: the architect's schedules set no U-value and defer - 'MIN. THERMAL RATING: To Edward Pearce Consulting Engineers specification' - and EDWARD PEARCE WROTE THE ENERGY STATEMENT (title block: 'Edward Pearce, Old School House, 35 Ewell Road, Surbiton, Surrey KT6 6AF, Project No. 22/190, February 2025, Revision 02'). Project 22/190 is the same number as every M&E document in the pack - the 22190-M01..M32 and 22190-E01..E25 drawings, the 140-page mech spec, the 127-page electrical spec and the drainage spec - so Edward Pearce are the appointed services and energy consultant and the deferral points at a document we already hold. GOVERNING FIGURES: GLAZING 1.10 W/m2K. Edward Pearce's headline is 'The external glazing will be replaced or improved to achieve a U-value of 1.1 W/m2K' and their existing-to-proposed comparison tables show glazing 1.60 -> 1.10 in both scenarios, with the proposed new flats at 1.10 and Opaque Door 1.00. (An intermediate retained-flats specification table shows 1.40 with vision-element g-value 0.40; the headline and the comparison tables agree on 1.10, so 1.10 is the figure.) 1.10 is TIGHTER than NBS L10 cl.330's 'U-value maximum 1.2 W/m2K' and it governs because the schedules expressly defer thermal rating to Edward Pearce. G-VALUE 0.36. The architect's schedules state 'G-Value of 0.36 or better' DIRECTLY, against Edward Pearce's 0.40. A directly stated requirement beats a deferred one, so 0.36 governs the g-value while 1.10 governs the U-value. DOORS: NBS L20 cl.280's 1.2 W/m2K remains the door-specific figure. Edward Pearce's 'Opaque Door 1.00' does NOT apply to our three FD30 doors, because in SAP an opaque door is a solid door and ours are glazed (EI30 Clear DGU) - glazed doors sit under glazing at 1.10. Not claiming a 1.00 door requirement. STILL OUTSTANDING (RFI-7, narrowed): NBS cl.330 also defers g-value, frame factor and glazing details to a 'SAP Consultants specification'. Edward Pearce ARE the SAP consultant ('Design SAP 10 and IES VE', 'Baseline SAP and SBEM calculations', 'the SAP 10 methodology') but their own document says 'Full SAP calculations for each scenario and the GLA reporting spreadsheet will be submitted in a separate file' - so the calculations are expressly held separately and are not in the pack. That is a request to a named party for a document known to exist, not an unowned question.
u_value.note: SM5 WEXHAM RULE APPLIED AND NOTHING IS REJECTED - deliberately. The Energy Statement's 1.1 is written as a general target for 'the external glazing' with no per-element or area-weighted wording, and there is no Uw stated on ANY of the four BSW quotes to test against it. I cannot compute the package average either, because a whole-window Uw exists for exactly one element on the job (the AFS fire doors' EI30 DGU at U=1.0, and that is a glass Ug too). St Mary's rule cuts both ways - do the arithmetic before you raise a finding OR drop it - and here the arithmetic cannot be done from what is on file. So the honest finding is not 'we fail 1.1', it is 'nothing on file demonstrates 1.1 and nobody has asked'. The open item is an RFI to BSW for whole-window Uw figures on the Liniar, Alunet and Sheerline elements, and confirmation of whose specification governs - the Energy Statement or Edward Pearce Consulting Engineers, whose spec the schedules defer to and which is NOT in the tender pack. SECOND TURN UPDATE - THE NBS NUMBERS CHANGE THE SHAPE OF THIS. Last turn the honest position was 'the schedules set no U-value at all', which made it look as though only the sustainability annex asked for anything - the exact escape route St Mary's warned about, where a client says the energy appendix does not apply to our package. It does not hold here: the NBS specification itself sets 1.2 W/m2K maximum on windows AND on communal entrance doors, so a thermal requirement exists in the governing technical document and does not depend on the Energy Statement at all. That is the St Mary's door-schedule lesson repeating - the requirement was in a third place nobody had opened. Still nothing to compute with: no BSW quote states a whole-window Uw, so nothing is rejected here either. The AFS fire doors are the only element with any stated figure (glass Ug 1.0) and even they carry no whole-door Ud against clause 280's 1.2. TWELFTH TURN: the deferral is resolved and the numbers are settled - 1.10 W/m2K glazing (Edward Pearce) and g-value 0.36 (architect). What has NOT changed is that no BSW quote states a whole-window Uw, so there is still nothing to test the 1.10 against; the requirement is now certain while our compliance remains unevidenced. RIVERSIDE'S DISTINCTION, WORTH KEEPING: a deferral to a NAMED, APPOINTED consultant whose other work is in the pack is an ADMINISTRATIVE gap - ask for the document. A deferral to nobody (their job names no structural engineer at all) is a DESIGN gap. Same wording on the drawing, entirely different problem, and only the second should stop you pricing.
